title: Microsoft Teams: voice phishing detection for external calls
summary: The roadmap facts and the documented PowerShell control are supported. The page correctly distinguishes the parameter's default from an unconfirmed rollout default and notes that the setting currently has no effect. A minor correction should acknowledge differing Microsoft documentation about the licences for separate call reporting.

The MicrosoftTeams PowerShell call Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -VoicePhishingDetection None sets the named policy's alert mode to None.
claims.quote:
Use this cmdlet to update values in existing Teams Calling Policies.
[-Identity] <string>
[-VoicePhishingDetection <string>]
**None**: No alerts.

claims.claim: VoicePhishingDetection is configured per calling policy and governs the experience of users covered by that policy.
claims.quote: The Teams Calling Policy controls which calling and call forwarding features are available to users in Microsoft Teams. This cmdlet allows admins to set values in a given Calling Policy instance.

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference describes AI-based voice phishing detection during live inbound Teams calls.
claims.quote: The Voice Phishing Detection policy enables AI-based detection of voice phishing (vishing) attempts during live inbound Microsoft Teams calls.

claims.where: summary; controls[0].note; What's changing; Why it matters; Scope: Rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The feature is not fully released and the setting currently has no effect, including when set to None.
claims.quote: This feature has not been fully released yet, so the setting will have no effect.

claims.claim: New-CsTeamsCallingPolicy also exposes VoicePhishingDetection with the same modes.
claims.quote:
### -VoicePhishingDetection
Possible values are:
- **BannerAndAudio**: Both visual and voice alerts when a voice phishing attempt is detected.
- **Banner**: Visual alert only.
- **Audio**: Voice alert only.
- **None**: No alerts.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The described feature warns the recipient; the sources describe no autonomous blocking or ending of calls.
claims.quote: Searched: "voice phishing detection" Teams; "voice phishing" Teams outbound "Scam Suspected" tenant switch group assignment. Read roadmap and Set/New-CsTeamsCallingPolicy: alerts and recipient decisions are described, not call termination.

claims.claim: The separate end user reporting for Teams Calling page is marked Preview.
claims.quote: # End user reporting for Teams Calling (Preview)

claims.claim: The cited calling-reporting page describes reporting in organisations with Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 or Defender XDR.
claims.quote: In organizations with Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 or Microsoft Defender XDR, admins can decide whether users can report malicious or suspicious calls in Microsoft Teams.
claims.fix: After the reporting licence sentence, add: 'Microsoft's User reported settings in Microsoft Teams page also includes Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 for call reporting.' Cite and add https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-office-365/submissions-teams to sources; that page says 'Plan 1 or Plan 2, or Microsoft Defender XDR'.

claims.claim: The Report call setting in a Teams calling policy controls whether users can report suspicious calls.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams Admin Center, go to **Voice > Calling policies**.
Select a policy.
Turn on the setting: **Report call**.

claims.claim: Reporting also needs to be enabled in Defender for user-reported calls to show up correctly.
claims.quote: If user reporting of calls is turned on in the Teams admin center, it also needs to be turned on in the Defender portal for user reported calls to show up correctly.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Users can report a call incorrectly flagged as Scam Suspected as not a security concern.
claims.quote:
In the Teams call history, locate the call that incorrectly flagged as "Scam Suspected".
Hover over the call without selecting it.
Select **...** > **Report as not a security concern**.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether this voice phishing detector produces the Scam Suspected flag.
claims.quote: Searched: "voice phishing" Teams outbound "Scam Suspected" tenant switch group assignment. Read call-reporting page, submissions-teams and Set/New-CsTeamsCallingPolicy; no passage links this detector to that flag.

claims.claim: The sources do not resolve outbound external-call coverage: the roadmap says external one-to-one calls and the reference says live inbound calls.
claims.quote: Searched: "voice phishing" "Teams" "outbound". Read roadmap and Set/New-CsTeamsCallingPolicy: external one-to-one and live inbound are their respective terms; no outbound coverage clarification found.

claims.claim: Teams calling policies control which calling and call-forwarding features are available to users.
claims.quote: In Microsoft Teams, calling policies control which calling and call forwarding features are available to users.

claims.quote: Microsoft Teams Phone supports a wide array of features that you control by policy. ... Policies can be applied at a global, group, and user level.

claims.quote: Searched: "VoicePhishingDetection" "tenant"; "VoicePhishingDetection" Graph API tenant configuration; "VoicePhishingDetection" "admin center". Read calling policies, settings reference and Set/New references; no separate switch or other setting surface found.
